Flags: ghost_coach_defaulted. Review pricing, coach, and injuries. # Training Approach — Joshua Botha ## Starting Phase: Hybridize Joshua enters **Phase 1 — Hybridize**. This is the foundation phase. Joint armor and mobility lead. Strength technique on the main lifts. Aerobic base building. Lower running volume at the start to allow muscle gain, higher mobility work to keep joints bulletproof. The goal here is to build the base that lets him add size while introducing running in a way that supports muscle gain instead of burning it off. Recommended for most new clients, especially those restarting after a layoff. --- ## Training Split: Hybrid 4-Day v1 — Upper / Lower × 2 **Library reference:** §10.1 Hybrid Training (general purpose) — Hybrid 4-day v1 Joshua trains 4 days lifting, 2 days running per week. This split balances upper-body aesthetics (broad shoulders, wide back, chest development) with lower-body strength maintenance and controlled aerobic work. The split structure is: - **Lifting days:** 4 per week (2 upper, 2 lower) - **Running days:** 2 per week (easy Z2 base building only for the first 4 weeks — no long-distance volume until Week 5+) - **Rest/active recovery:** 1 full rest day (Sunday) - **Session order:** Lift first, run second on any double days (rare in this phase) - **Interference management:** Running volume stays LOW in Weeks 1–4 to prioritise muscle gain. No quality runs (tempo, intervals, hills) until Week 5. B1 lower session sits Wednesday with 48+ hours before Sunday's easy run. No VO2 or threshold work the day after heavy lower-body lifting. Joshua's concern about running making him skinny is real — his metabolism is fast, and his past experience (30 km/week with no structured nutrition = weight loss) proves it. The fix: cap running at 15–20 km/week max in Phase 1, all easy Z2, and layer it in AFTER the muscle base is established. Week 1 = zero running. Week 2 = one 20-min easy jog. Week 3 = two 25-min easy jogs. By Week 5, when upper-body size is visibly up and nutrition is locked in, we add one longer Z2 run (45–60 min) on Sunday. Running becomes a tool for cardiovascular health and work capacity, not a weight-loss mechanism. --- ## Week 1 Ignition Protocol **Activation point:** Visible mirror change (pump + posture) + energy/sleep transformation combo. Joshua's top pain points from the call: energy levels, motivation, discipline, consistency. He's also aesthetic-driven — "nice broad shoulders, nice back, nice chest, swimmer-type look." The ignition protocol targets BOTH energy transformation (sleep, daily vitality, training drive) AND a visible upper-body pump by day 7. This dual activation locks him in psychologically faster than scale weight alone (which he wants UP, not down). **7-Day Target Metrics:** - Visible: Upper-body pump noticeable in mirror and T-shirt fit by day 7 — chest, shoulders, arms fuller. - Energy: Reports "waking up easier" and "more energy during the day" by check-in 1 (day 7). - Performance: Completes all 4 lifting sessions in Week 1 without skipping — proof of newfound consistency. ### Week 1 Session Structure (library codes): Day · Session **Mon** · A1 — Upper Hypertrophy-Strength (60 min) + M2 T-Spine + Shoulder attached (10 min post-lift) **Tue** · Off / walk 20–30 min (active recovery, no structured run yet) **Wed** · B1 — Lower Strength-Retention (55 min) + M1 Hip + Ankle Armor attached (12 min post-lift) **Thu** · Off / walk 20–30 min **Fri** · A2 — Upper Maintenance + Arm Emphasis (50 min) + M2 attached (8 min) **Sat** · B3 — Lower Neural Maintenance (40 min) — lighter lower to avoid fatigue bleed into next week **Sun** · M4 5-min daily minimum + walk 30 min (full active recovery) **Why this works for activation:** - **Two upper days (Mon A1 + Fri A2) front-loaded** = chest, shoulders, and arms get hit TWICE in 5 days with high-quality volume and direct arm supersets. Pump is visible by Friday night. T-shirt fit changes by Sunday. - **Two lower days (Wed B1 + Sat B3)** = strength foundation locked in, legs get work, but Sat B3 is neural (light, crisp, non-fatiguing) so there's no residual soreness bleeding into Week 2. - **Zero running in Week 1** = all energy and recovery capacity goes toward lifting and muscle gain. Joshua's fast metabolism means we protect every calorie for anabolism this week. Running starts Week 2 only. - **Mobility flows attached to every lifting day** = M1 (hips/ankles) after lower, M2 (t-spine/shoulders) after upper, M4 daily minimum on rest days. This builds the joint armor habit from day one and reduces injury risk when running volume ramps later. **Nutrition lever paired with Week 1 ignition (cross-reference Output 2):** - Aggressive calorie surplus (\~500 kcal above maintenance, \~3,200 kcal/day to start). - High carbs (\~350 g) timed around training = glycogen-driven pump + energy spike. - Protein anchored to goal weight (82 kg target = \~180 g/day). - Sodium front-loaded around sessions (salty pre-workout meal) = intramuscular water retention = fuller look in mirror. - Creatine loaded (20 g/day Week 1, then 5 g maintenance) = immediate cell volumisation. - Post-workout carb + protein within 60 min every session = glycogen repletion + anabolic window captured. - Sleep optimisation: magnesium + zinc at night, no caffeine post-3pm, 8-hour non-negotiable. **Check-in moment:** Day 7 (Sunday end-of-week check-in). Capture: - Front-relaxed mirror photo (same lighting as day 1) — compare pump and T-shirt fit. - Subjective energy rating 1–10 (compare to baseline). - Confirm all 4 lifting sessions completed (proof of consistency). - Weight (we WANT it up 1–2 kg this week from glycogen + water + food volume — this is the win, not a loss). If activation lands (visible pump + energy up + all 4 sessions done), frame it in the first check-in: \*"You've banked the first proof point. If you've come this far in 7 days, imagine 12 weeks."\* This is the seed for the 30-day vision and the renewal conversation at Month 5. --- ## Weekly Layout (Sample Week — Mid-Block, Week 5+) By Week 5, running is layered in at controlled volume. Weekly structure stabilises here and repeats for 8–12 weeks with progressive overload on marquee lifts and gradual run-distance increases. Day · AM · PM **Mon** · A1 — Upper Hypertrophy-Strength (60 min) + M2 attached · — **Tue** · — · R1 — Easy Z2 (30 min) **Wed** · B1 — Lower Strength-Retention (55 min) + M1 attached · — **Thu** · — · R1 — Easy Z2 (30 min) **Fri** · A2 — Upper Maintenance + Arm Emphasis (50 min) · — **Sat** · B3 — Lower Neural Maintenance (40 min) OR Catalyst Conditioning (base session, 30 min — alternate weekly) · — **Sun** · — · R2 — Long Z2 (60 min, building to 75 min by Week 12) **Session codes mapped:** - **A1** = main upper growth day (incline barbell press marquee, chin-ups, rows, direct arm supersets, delts). - **A2** = lower-fatigue upper (incline DB press marquee, cable rows, arm emphasis via lengthened curls + triceps). - **B1** = main lower strength day (back squat OR trap-bar deadlift alternate weekly, RDL, Bulgarian split squat, leg curls, calves, core). - **B3** = neural maintenance lower (trap-bar deadlift light and crisp, split squats, calves, plank — keeps strength switched on without fatiguing legs before Sunday long run). - **R1** = easy Z2 base run (30 min, conversational pace, nose-breathing dominant). - **R2** = long Z2 (60–75 min, fully aerobic, the cornerstone run for aerobic base and endurance). - **M1** = Hip + Ankle Armor (attached post-lower). - **M2** = T-Spine + Shoulder (attached post-upper). - **M4** = 5-min daily minimum (Joshua does this every morning before work from Week 2 onward as a non-negotiable habit anchor). **Why this works:** - Upper and lower each get 48+ hr recovery. A1 Mon → B1 Wed → A2 Fri → B3 Sat = clean spacing, no interference. - Easy runs Tue/Thu sit between lifting days with no leg fatigue bleed. Both are short (30 min), fully aerobic, recovery-enhancing. - Long run Sun sits 24+ hr after Sat B3 (which is light neural work, not hypertrophy), so legs are fresh. If Sat is a Conditioning day instead, it's base-level (low-intensity mixed-modal), also non-fatiguing. - **Total weekly running volume by Week 8:** \~20 km (2 × 30 min + 1 × 60 min). This is HALF what Joshua ran before (30 km/week = the volume that made him skinny). At 20 km/week with aggressive surplus nutrition, he gains muscle while building aerobic base. Volume can creep to 25 km by Week 12 if body composition stays on track, but never exceeds that in Hybridize. **Constraint-driven swaps:** - **Travel week:** Swap A1 + B1 for C3 Hotel / No-Gym Full Body (30–40 min, tempo split squats, feet-elevated push-ups, single-leg RDL with backpack, band rows, band curls + triceps). Swap A2 for C3.b Hotel Push-Bias. Keep one easy run (hotel treadmill or local park). Drop long run if travel is short (under 4 days). - **Work overload week (12-hour days):** Compress A1 to 50 min via supersets (pair accessory curls + triceps, lateral raises + calves). Drop Sat B3 entirely, keep A1/B1/A2 only. Run frequency drops to 1× (Sun long Z2 only, cut to 45 min). This is the "minimum effective dose" week — still progressing, not maintaining. - **Moving week (this week, 2026-09-28):** Zero lifting Mon–Wed while sorting apartment. Resume Thu with A2 (upper light, 45 min) to test energy. Fri = walk only. Sat = B3 if recovered, otherwise M1 mobility flow standalone. Sun = R1 easy 20-min jog or walk if still settling in. Week 1 ignition protocol STARTS the week Joshua confirms he's fully moved in and ready to commit (likely 2026-10-01 or 2026-10-02). --- ## Conditioning Prescription Conditioning is optional in Hybridize unless the client requests it or the split prescribes it. For Joshua, conditioning sits as a **Sat alternate** starting Week 5: one week B3 lower neural, next week Catalyst Conditioning base session (30 min). This keeps weekly training stimulus varied without overloading recovery. **Prescription:** \*"Catalyst Conditioning workout — pick one from the base category."\* Joshua opens \`catalyst-conditioning-playbook.md\` (stored in Everfit library) and selects a 30-min base session — steady aerobic work, low intensity, mixed-modal (e.g. row + bike + sled drag, all Z2 pace). No EMOM, no AMRAP, no threshold work in Hybridize. Conditioning here is active recovery with a cardio touch, not a suffer-fest. If Joshua wants Hyrox-style work later (Phase 2 Execute or Phase 3 Reshape), conditioning prescription shifts to engine and race-specific sessions. Not relevant in Hybridize. --- ## Mobility / Joint Armor Joshua's joint health rating = 10/10. No current injuries. But he's restarting after 2+ years of inconsistency, and he'll be running again. Mobility is PREVENTATIVE, not reactive. **Flows attached:** - **M1 — Hip + Ankle Armor:** Attached post-B1 (Wed) and standalone Sun mornings before long run (from Week 5 onward). 10–12 min. Bulletproofs the runner's foundation. Especially critical given Joshua will layer in 20+ km/week by mid-block. - **M2 — T-Spine + Shoulder:** Attached post-A1 (Mon) and post-A2 (Fri). 8–10 min. Opens thoracic spine, restores shoulder rotation, sets upper body up for clean pressing and pulling. Given Joshua's goal is "broad shoulders, nice back, nice chest," keeping the shoulder girdle healthy is non-negotiable. - **M3 — Knee Resilience:** Not prescribed unless a knee flag surfaces. Joshua has no knee issues currently. Hold this in reserve. If he reports any knee discomfort once running ramps (unlikely given the controlled volume), slot M3 as a standalone session Sat or before B1 Wed. - **M4 — 5-Min Daily Minimum:** Prescribed as a **daily habit anchor starting Week 2**. Joshua does this every morning before work (7:00 AM, pre-breakfast, 5 min). Non-negotiable. Builds joint quality on autopilot. The five exercises: 90/90 hip switch, world's greatest stretch, cat-cow, tib raise, wall slides. This is the single highest-ROI mobility investment in the system — 5 min/day = 35 min/week = 140 min/month of joint armor for near-zero time cost. **Why mobility matters here:** Joshua's biggest constraint is CONSISTENCY. Mobility flows are short (5–12 min), require no equipment, and can be done anywhere (apartment gym, hotel room, office floor). They don't feel like "training," so they're psychologically easier to execute on low-motivation days. And they reduce injury risk as running volume ramps, which protects the consistency streak. A single injury = 2–3 weeks off = the pattern he's trying to break. Mobility is the insurance policy. --- ## Constraint Management ### Key constraints extracted: 1. **Fast metabolism** — loses weight quickly when running volume is high. 2. **Time-poor** — 9-to-5 sales job + 3:30–6 PM trading window + gym after 6 PM. 3. **Moving week (current)** — apartment transition, reduced training capacity this week. 4. **Girlfriend's family dinners** — eats at Scarlett's family home "majority of the time" = less control over meal composition. 5. **No current training partner** — training solo, no external accountability except coach. ### Adaptations per constraint: **1. Fast metabolism:** - Running volume CAPPED at 20 km/week in Hybridize (Weeks 1–12). Never exceeds 25 km/week even in Execute unless body composition is ahead of schedule. - All runs in Hybridize are easy Z2 or recovery pace (R1, R2, R8). Zero tempo, zero intervals, zero hills until Phase 2. Aerobic work supports muscle gain via improved nutrient partitioning and work capacity, but only if volume and intensity stay controlled. - Nutrition layered to OVERFEED on lifting days and long-run days (Output 2 details this). Surplus is aggressive (\~500 kcal above maintenance). Protein high (180 g/day anchored to 82 kg goal weight, NOT current 71 kg). Carbs timed around training (pre-workout + post-workout within 60 min = anabolic window captured). - Weekly weigh-ins track trend. Target = +0.3–0.5 kg/week in Weeks 1–8 (muscle gain + glycogen + water). If weight stalls or drops for 2 consecutive weeks, bump calories +200 immediately and reassess running volume (cut one R1 session if needed). If weight spikes \>1 kg/week for 2 consecutive weeks, hold calories steady and let body composition catch up (likely water + glycogen, not fat, given Joshua's metabolism). **2. Time-poor (sales + trading + gym):** - All lifting sessions compressed to 50–60 min max via supersets and giant sets. No session exceeds 70 min. Marquee lift always protected (never dropped), but accessory pairings are compressed when time is tight. - Running sessions SHORT in Hybridize: 30 min Tue/Thu, 60 min Sun. Total weekly time cost = 2 hr running + 3.5 hr lifting = 5.5 hr/week. Fits inside Joshua's "3–5 hours/week" commitment from the call. - Mobility flows attach to existing sessions (post-lift), not standalone, so they don't add separate time blocks. M4 5-min daily is pre-work (7:05 AM, before breakfast), so it doesn't compete with evening gym window. - Saturday session (B3 or Conditioning) is optional if the week gets crushed. Drop it first. Core week = Mon A1 + Wed B1 + Fri A2 + Sun R2. If Joshua only hits those 4, he still progresses. **3. Moving week (current, 2026-09-28):** - Zero structured training Mon–Wed (2026-09-28 to 2026-09-30) while sorting apartment. Walk 20–30 min daily if energy allows, otherwise full rest. - Resume Thu 2026-10-03 with A2 (upper light, 45 min) as a test session. If energy is good, continue normal schedule Fri onward. If energy is still low, delay Week 1 ignition protocol start to Mon 2026-10-07. - Brandon (ghost coach) flags this in the Coach Playbook: \*"Joshua is mid-move this week (2026-09-28). Expect delayed start. Confirm with him by Fri 2026-10-04 when he's ready to lock in Week 1 ignition. Do not push hard until he signals readiness — he's already committed, let him settle first."\* **4. Girlfriend's family dinners:** - Nutrition ecosystem (Output 2) builds around this. Scarlett's family meals get reverse-engineered: ask Joshua what they typically cook (he mentioned spaghetti bolognese as a favourite), calculate macros, give him portion guidance and a pre-meal or post-meal top-up strategy to hit daily targets. - Example: Family serves spaghetti bolognese (carb-heavy, moderate protein, low fat). Joshua eats a normal portion (no weird behaviour at the table), then tops up protein post-dinner with a shake or Greek yoghurt + berries at home. Macros hit, no social friction. - Dining out / date nights: Output 2 includes ordering playbooks for 4 environments (at home, Uber Eats, restaurants, travel). Joshua gets 3–5 concrete "order this" options per environment using HIS favourite foods (pizza, restaurant pasta, McDonald's burger, Mexican bowl). Nothing is banned by default. Every food he loves that can fit the macros gets a place. **5. No training partner:** - Weekly check-ins (Mon/Tue/Wed, his choice) become the accountability anchor. Brandon (ghost coach) replies same-day if submitted by 5 PM. - WhatsApp community group (he mentioned liking this on the call) gives him peer accountability and "boys" energy even though he's training solo. - Weekly coach call (optional but encouraged) — Brandon runs calls Tue + Sat. Joshua can book in 1× per week if he wants the face-to-face touch. Not mandatory, but useful for motivation spikes when consistency wavers. - Everfit app daily check-in habit: Joshua logs every session (even just "Done" + top-set weight for marquee lift). Brandon sees it in real-time. If 48 hr pass with no log, Brandon messages proactively: \*"Josh, you good? Haven't seen a session log since Wed. What's up?"\* This catches the slip BEFORE it becomes a ghost week. --- ## Performance Benchmarks ### 4-Week Milestone (= 30-Day Vision) The 4-week milestone IS the 30-day vision locked in Step 2.5. State targets explicitly across all three pillars: **Visible body change:** - Front-relaxed mirror photo shows fuller chest, broader shoulders, more defined arms vs. baseline. - T-shirt fit noticeably tighter through upper body (chest, shoulders, arms). - Scale weight: 73–74 kg (up 2–3 kg from 71 kg start — muscle + glycogen + water, NOT fat). **Body composition shift:** - **Marquee lift PRs (library session codes cited):** - A1 incline barbell press: 60 kg × 6 reps (top set, RPE 8.5) — up from estimated 50 kg × 6 baseline. - B1 back squat OR trap-bar deadlift: 100 kg × 6 reps (top set, RPE 8.5) — up from estimated 80 kg × 6 baseline. - A2 incline DB press: 32 kg DBs × 8 reps (top set, RPE 8) — up from estimated 26 kg DBs × 8 baseline. - Measurement target: Upper-arm circumference +1 cm (measure cold, unflexed, mid-bicep). Chest circumference +2 cm (measure across nipple line, relaxed). Waist stable or down 1 cm (we're gaining muscle, not fat). **Performance benchmark:** - R2 long Z2 (Sun): Completes 60 min continuously at conversational pace without stopping. Pace doesn't matter yet (likely 6:30–7:00/km given he's rebuilding base), but COMPLETION without walking = the win. This proves aerobic base is building and he's not "losing fitness" despite lower run frequency than his old 30 km/week habit. - Energy and lifestyle: Reports "waking up easier," "more energy during the day," "training 4×/week feels automatic now" in Week 4 check-in. Consistency streak = 16/16 lifting sessions completed in 4 weeks (4 sessions/week × 4 weeks, zero skips). **How we measure:** - Photos: Front relaxed, side relaxed, back relaxed (same time of day, same lighting, same location). Submitted Week 4 check-in. - Scale weight: Logged Mon AM every week (post-bathroom, pre-food, minimal clothing). Trend tracked in Everfit. - Lifts: Top-set weight + reps logged every session for A1 incline press, B1 squat/deadlift, A2 incline DB press. Everfit auto-tracks PRs. - Run completion: R2 long Z2 distance + time logged in Everfit. Week 4 target = 60 min completed. - Subjective markers: Energy rating 1–10 (tracked in weekly check-in). Consistency streak visible in Everfit calendar (green = session logged, red = missed). --- ### 8-Week Milestone **Body composition:** - Scale weight: 76–77 kg (up 5–6 kg from start, still lean — abs visible but not shredded, upper body noticeably bigger). - Visible: "Swimmer's body" clearly emerging — broad shoulders, wide back, chest developed, arms filling out T-shirt sleeves. Still lean enough to see top 4 abs. No love handles, no gut (Joshua's natural leanness + controlled surplus = aesthetic gain, not fat spillover). **Lifting (marquee lifts, by session code):** - A1 incline barbell press: 67.5 kg × 6 reps (top set, RPE 8.5) — up 7.5 kg from Week 4. - B1 back squat OR trap-bar deadlift: 110 kg × 6 reps — up 10 kg from Week 4. - A2 incline DB press: 36 kg DBs × 8 reps — up 4 kg DBs from Week 4. **Running (by run code):** - R2 long Z2: 75 min completed continuously at Z2 pace (\~6:15–6:30/km, pace dropping as aerobic base improves). No walking breaks. - R1 easy Z2: 30 min feels "easy" — conversational throughout, heart rate stable in Z2, recovery rapid. - Total weekly run volume: 22–23 km (2 × 30 min + 1 × 75 min). Joshua is running MORE than Week 4 but NOT losing weight because nutrition is dialled and lifting stimulus is strong. **Energy and lifestyle:** - Consistency streak: 32/32 lifting sessions (8 weeks × 4 sessions/week, zero skips). - Sleep: 8 hr/night consistently (tracked via Everfit daily log or subjective report). - Energy rating: 8–9/10 most days. No afternoon crashes. Trading window (3:30–6 PM) no longer feels sluggish. - Social proof: Scarlett or family comments on visible physique change ("you're looking strong again"). Joshua mentions this in Week 8 check-in = renewal trigger signal (unsolicited praise). --- ### 12-Week Milestone (End of Hybridize Block) **Body composition:** - Scale weight: 78–80 kg (up 7–9 kg from start). Abs still visible (not shredded but defined top 4). Upper body substantially bigger — chest, shoulders, back all noticeably wider. Arms filling out shirt sleeves. Legs thicker but not bulky (functional strength, not bodybuilder quads). - Body fat estimate: 12–14% (lean enough to see abs, thick enough to look strong and athletic — exactly the "swimmer's body" aesthetic Joshua described on the call). **Lifting (marquee lifts, by session code):** - A1 incline barbell press: 75 kg × 6 reps (top set, RPE 8.5) — up 15 kg from baseline (50 kg × 6 estimated), 7.5 kg from Week 8. - B1 back squat OR trap-bar deadlift: 120 kg × 6 reps — up 40 kg from baseline (80 kg × 6 estimated), 10 kg from Week 8. - A2 incline DB press: 40 kg DBs × 8 reps — up 14 kg DBs from baseline (26 kg DBs × 8 estimated), 4 kg DBs from Week 8. - All accessory lifts progressed similarly (rows, chin-ups, RDLs, split squats, curls, triceps). Everfit tracks full history. Marquee lifts are the headline numbers. **Running (by run code):** - R2 long Z2: 90 min completed continuously at Z2 pace (\~6:00–6:15/km, aerobic base substantially improved). Conversational throughout. No fatigue bleed into Monday A1 upper session. - R1 easy Z2: 35 min, feels like active recovery (heart rate mid-Z2, breathing relaxed, could run longer if needed). - R8 recovery + strides: Introduced Week 10. 25 min easy jog + 6 × 20-sec strides at fast-but-relaxed pace. Sharpens neuromuscular speed without fatigue cost. Joshua enjoys this — feels athletic, not grinding. - Total weekly run volume: 25 km (2 × 35 min + 1 × 90 min). This is STILL below his old 30 km/week habit, but he's 8 kg heavier, visibly bigger, and aerobically fitter than he was at 30 km/week before.
